provenance: New source translation; E4310-E4319 and E4400-E4409 reviewed.
context: Fiore opens Zalm, Tong and Schol boxes. Shadow riddle and unavoidable Schol wordplay traps.
decisions: Schol wordplay depends on Japanese kana; retain both trap choices and explicitly describe Japanese pronunciation changes. No choice/parser rewriting. Sole/flatfish face directions preserved as source depicts them.

translations.en: Ding ding ding!
Correct! The answer is your shadow.
It's stuck to your feet and such all day long, isn't it?
Always right there beside you.
Now, open!
Inside the box were countless glass fragments,
the shattered remains of what must once have been beautiful glasswork.
What a waste!
It must have been worth a lot before it broke...
Could we use it for something?
I'll take these pieces back for now.
Yes, the sun's always there.
But that's wrong! Bzzzt!
The sun doesn't stay close beside you, does it?
It's not right next to you.
This friend might be in front or behind,
but it's always close by your side.
A salmon was drawn on the box,
with the word Zalm carved beneath it.
Hello, hello! Salmon are fish that return after a long journey.
Did you know that?
Well, yes...
I see. If you hadn't, I'd have spent a whole day
telling you a tale so moving that teller and listener alike would weep.
But I suppose I won't tell it now.
If you want the box opened, answer my question.
A friend? Following you even when you're alone?
Are you talking about some supernatural phenomenon?
Bzzzt! It's nothing supernatural.
Now, answer the question!
A fish was drawn on a box, both eyes facing left.
Was it a flounder? The word Tong was carved beneath it.
Tong Box
Speak to me if you like. I have no intention of answering.
For anyone who tries to open me without the proper key
is a scoundrel, every last one!
The box chanted a spell!
The party's HP was halved!
It had a guardian,
so there has to be something good inside, right?
Eyes shining with anticipation, @7rFiore@0r opened the box
to find a pile of decorative plates painted with flounders.
Decorative plates... with flounders?
What am I supposed to do with dishes like these?!
No, no, no. Wait, wait, wait.
Maybe there's a collector out there who likes this sort of thing.
Some old appraiser might say, "Such fine craftsmanship."
Let's take them back anyway.
There was a box with a flatfish drawn on it.
It faced right, so it was surely a righteye flounder.
The word Schol was carved beneath it.
Schol Box
Change my name a little, and it becomes something else.
Add a circle to its Japanese spelling, or remove something:
either way, it becomes a foreign word and sets something different in motion.
Will you add a circle
or remove something?
Do we have to choose one?
Yes. You must choose one to proceed.
Fate always demands a choice between two paths.
Now, which will it be?
Add a circle
Remove something
You'll add a circle?
A circle changes ho to po in my Japanese name: suhooru becomes supooru.
translations.note: Japanese kana wordplay explicitly explained; result supooru has unclear foreign etymology. Both options trigger mandatory traps; no parser literals changed.

translations.en: That is a word for exercise in another tongue.
translations.note: Source explicitly calls supooru a foreign word for exercise; no confident source language identified. Literal gloss retained; functional trap choice unaffected.

translations.en: Exercise means moving your body.
And moving your body means fighting!
Come forth, monsters who protect me!
You'll remove something?
Remove su from my Japanese name, suhooru, and you get hooru.
Hooru means "hole."
And a hole means a trap!
A pit shall now open beneath your feet!
Now I shall unlock myself.
Look upon my contents.
What an arrogant box...
There'd better be something inside to justify it.
Inside was a set of rusty equipment.
Wha... Is that all?
